notes: NOTES: These figures plot the impacts of AI model deployment on log(resolutions per hour) for different groups of agents. Agent skill is calculated as the agent's trailing three month average of performance on average handle time, call resolution, and customer satisfaction, the three metrics our firm uses to assess agent performance. Within each month and company, agents are grouped into quintiles, with the most productive agents in quintile 5 and the least productive in quintile 1. Pre-AI worker tenure is the number of months an agent has been employed when they receive access to AI recommendations. All specifications include agent and chat year-month, location, and company fixed effects and standard errors are clustered at the agent level.

observations: Figure 6 contains two panels: Panel A shows impact by agent skill quintile at AI deployment; Panel B shows impact by agent tenure at AI deployment.
Both panels plot Log(Resolutions Per Hour) on y-axis (range approx -1 to 4), with error bars indicating confidence intervals.
In Panel A, highest skill (Q5) shows smallest positive/near-zero impact; lowest skill (Q1) shows largest positive impact.
In Panel B, shortest tenure (0 Mos.) shows largest positive impact; longest tenure (>12 Mos.) shows near-zero or slightly negative impact.
All data points are point estimates with vertical error bars; no numerical values are labeled on the plots—only approximate positions inferred from axis gridlines.
uncertainties: Exact numerical values for Log(Resolutions Per Hour) and error bar bounds are not printed on the figure; only approximate values can be inferred from visual grid alignment.
The y-axis label 'Log(Resolutions Per Hour)' is truncated in Panel B as 'Log(Resolutions Per Hour)' with a visible '-1' tick at bottom, but full range not explicitly labeled beyond gridlines.
No table of raw coefficients or standard errors is provided; all values are extracted visually from scatter/error-bar plot.
The term 'Resolutions Per Hour' is not defined in units (e.g., whether it includes partial hours or is normalized); this is only described in notes as outcome metric.
